plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy since the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win but others bid high; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $13, I should bid exactly $13 to maximize expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own) if you win. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no repeated learning needed since values are redrawn independently, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $30.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy — it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you win exactly when your value exceeds the market price, and pay only the second-highest bid, not your own. There's no incentive to shade or inflate the bid. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $28.
